contract.settlement_definition: Three series, one team winner each. KXNBAALLSTARGAME (2026) settles Yes for the champion of the 'Pro Basketball All-Star Tournament': a round-robin mini-tournament of four 12-minute games among USA Stars, USA Stripes and World (Game 1 Stars v World, Game 2 Stripes v Game-1 winner, Game 3 Stripes v Game-1 loser, Game 4 the championship between the top two); if all three finish 1-1 the first tiebreaker is point differential across each team's two games. KXNBARISINGSTARS settles Yes for the winner of a four-team bracket 'originally scheduled for February 13, 2026': two semifinals won by the first team to reach or exceed 40 points and a championship to 25. KXNBAALLSTAR (2025, 'Shaq's OGs') has a one-line primary rule and empty secondary text, so its format, ties and team changes are not in Kalshi's text. Nothing sampled names a source of truth, the tiebreaker after point differential, overtime inside a tied 12-minute game, or the treatment of a team that cannot field a roster.

rules_evidence.quote: The Pro Basketball All-Star Game will feature a round-robin mini-tournament with four 12-minute games.
rules_evidence.establishes: 2026 game market is a tournament champion market over timed 12-minute games, not a single game and not a target-score format.

rules_evidence.quote: If all three teams finish 1-1 after the round-robin games, the first tiebreaker will be point differential across each team’s two games.
rules_evidence.establishes: Margins, not only wins, matter for advancement; later tiebreakers (if point differential ties) are not stated.

rules_evidence.quote: Game 4: All-Star Championship (top two teams from round-robin play)
rules_evidence.establishes: A championship game between the top two round-robin teams decides the series; round-robin record alone does not settle it.

rules_evidence.quote: Semifinal games are won by the first team to reach or exceed 40 points, and the Championship is won by the first team to reach or exceed 25 points.
rules_evidence.establishes: Rising Stars uses target-score races (40 then 25), so a race-to-target model, not a margin-per-minute model, applies; the text does not say whether any time limit or overtime rule also exists.
The rule anticipates rescheduling: settlement follows the event even if moved; a cancellation path is not stated.

rules_evidence.quote: If Shaq's OGs wins the NBA All-Star Game, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The 2025 game market names a drafted team ('Shaq's OGs') and gives no format, tie or team-change text, so nothing about its structure is read from Kalshi; any target-score structure for 2025 would have to come from league material (unverified here).

variants_and_edge_cases: KXNBAALLSTARGAME 2026: point differential is the first tiebreaker only for a 1-1/1-1/1-1 round robin; the next tiebreaker and any overtime in a tied 12-minute game are not in Kalshi's text (the league rules sheet reportedly adds overtime if needed, relayed by web search, unread directly).

Seat effect: the team that sits out Game 1 (USA Stripes in 2026) plays Games 2 and 3, so its path is not symmetric with the other two; the 2026 result (Stripes 2-0, Stars 1-1, World 0-2, Stars won the final 47-21) is one sample.

KXNBAALLSTAR (2025) versus KXNBAALLSTARGAME (2026): same Kalshi contract family, but the 2025 format (named teams such as 'Shaq's OGs') is UNVERIFIED and was not researched, while 2026 is a timed round robin quoted from Kalshi; history cannot be pooled without a format vector, and margin or variance scales must never be pooled across formats of different length.

KXNBARISINGSTARS: semifinals end at the first team to reach or exceed 40 and the final at 25; the sampled text states no clock, time limit or overtime rule, so whether one exists is unknown (gap e5); the market names 'originally scheduled for' a date so postponement keeps it alive, while cancellation is unstated; the 2026 final finished 25-24 (secondary report).

Team identity: all three series name a team ('Team World', 'Team Vince', 'Shaq's OGs'); no clause says what happens if a team is renamed, merged or cannot be fielded, unlike the player series of the sibling archetypes.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in any sampled rule; assumed to be the NBA's official announcement of the champion (NBA.com results). Kalshi's own determination governs if it differs.

series_input_scope.KXNBAALLSTAR_note: Scope for KXNBAALLSTAR (2025) is provisional: its format is UNVERIFIED and unresearched, so the race model and the Rising Stars rating are excluded until the format is read.

mechanism.summary: An All-Star exhibition winner is produced in five steps. First, rosters are fixed by selection and assignment: fan, player, media and coach votes, a nationality split with Commissioner additions in 2026, honorary-coach drafts for Rising Stars and a G League side. Second, who actually plays and for how long is set by injuries, replacements and minute-sharing in games of only 12 minutes. Third, each side's scoring ability in a game with little defence comes from offensive talent, three-point volume and effort that fades or spikes late. Fourth, a single game converts the gap into a winner either through a timed margin with a large standard deviation or through a first-passage race to 40 or 25 points. Fifth, the tournament structure turns single-game results into a champion through pairings that depend on Game 1, a point-differential tiebreak when all three teams are 1-1, seeding to a final and a short final. Short, high-variance games cap favourites, so structure and format parameters matter about as much as roster strength, and no regular-season counting-stat machinery applies directly.

stages.name: Roster and team formation
stages.description: Rosters come from votes (starters by fans, players and media, reserves by coaches), a 2026 nationality rule that required at least 16 US and 8 international players with the Commissioner free to add players, honorary-coach drafts of seven-player Rising Stars teams plus a G League squad, and replacements for injured selectees. Who is on which team, and how deep the World side is against two US sides, is decided here before any game is played, and a replacement announced late changes a team's composite the day before.
stages.distribution: Discrete team membership; replacement is a Bernoulli per selectee with correlated risk for players who also appear in other weekend events.

stages.name: Who plays and for how many minutes
stages.description: Each game lasts one 12-minute period (plus overtime if needed, per a rules sheet relayed by search), so a single skipped shift removes a large share of a star's playing time, and coaches share minutes to keep everyone on the floor. A team that reaches the final plays two or three games in one evening, so minutes and fatigue accumulate unevenly, and a minor injury often means no appearance at all.
stages.distribution: Discrete minutes scenarios per player and game; correlated across a team through the coach's sharing rule; threshold behaviour at the injury-status tier.

stages.name: Offence-first scoring strength under minimal defence
stages.description: With little defensive effort, scoring is driven by shooting talent, three-point volume and creation of the players who are on the floor, not by defensive ratings, so the composite for a team is an offensive composite weighted by projected minutes. Rising Stars sides need a separate rating because first- and second-year players and G League players come from different leagues with different competition levels, and the evidence about each is thin and noisy.
stages.distribution: Approximately additive over players with shrinkage; cross-league ratings for Rising Stars have wide posterior spread.

stages.name: Single-game conversion: timed margin versus first-passage race
stages.description: A timed 12-minute game turns a team gap into a win probability through a margin with a large standard deviation, and late-game effort can compress variance; a target game ends the instant a team reaches 40 or 25 (the sampled text states no clock, time limit or overtime rule, which is unverified), so the winner is a first-passage event with discrete 1-, 2- and 3-point jumps and the final can end 25-24. The two regimes must be estimated separately, and effort must be treated as a regime parameter rather than a constant.
stages.distribution: Timed games: roughly normal margin with SD larger than a full game's per-minute scale; target games: first-passage race with discrete increments and an overshoot at the end.

stages.name: Tournament structure: pairings, tiebreak and seeding to the final
stages.description: In the 2026 All-Star round robin the Game 2 and Game 3 pairings depend on Game 1, the top two teams meet in Game 4, and a 1-1-1 outcome is settled by point differential, so margin chasing matters in exactly one branch; the Rising Stars bracket is two single-elimination semifinals to 40 and a final to 25. A Monte Carlo path simulation over the format vector gives P(champion) and P(final) per team, and it cannot be fitted on past champions because the format changed in 2026.
stages.distribution: Sequential multi-game path; champion distribution is a mixture over round-robin or bracket outcomes with a margin-sum dependence between games.

stages.name: Settlement of the champion
stages.description: Each series settles on the officially announced team champion. The sampled rules confirm the 2026 round-robin structure with the 1-1-1 point-differential tiebreak and the Rising Stars 40/25 targets, and are silent on later tiebreakers, overtime in a tied 12-minute game, a team that cannot be fielded and the 2025 format.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the official result; ambiguity mass sits in rare branches (later tiebreakers, ties, cancellation, renamed teams).

talent_strength.note: Offensive roster strength of each side, with a separate shrunk rating for Rising Stars.

opponent_matchup.note: Pairwise team margins and the pairing rule are the only matchups; there is no scheme interaction in a no-defence game.

role_personnel.note: Roster membership, nationality split and minute-sharing.

availability_news.note: Injuries, replacements and announcements before the weekend.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaches in the exhibitions only set rotations and minute sharing; there is no scheme.

environment.note: The venue is a neutral site chosen years ahead with no home team in the exhibitions, so no venue, altitude or travel input is warranted for the three series.

game_context_script.note: Round-robin margin incentives, race-to-target ends and timed late effort.

pace_volume.note: Exhibition pace and three-point volume by format regime.

efficiency_conversion.note: Offensive efficiency of the players on the floor inside the composite.

distribution_variance.note: Margin SD per 12 minutes, first-passage races and tournament-path mixtures.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Effort and motivation (prize money, home-market players, rivalry between nationality teams, doubling up with contests and Rising Stars) have no measurable pregame proxy defined for the exhibitions.

officiating_rules.note: Exhibition fouling is rare and referees do not shape a champion; the rule-sheet items that matter (game length, targets, tiebreakers) are format parameters held in the ledger, not officiating inputs.

settlement_contract.note: Rules sampled for all three series; KXNBAALLSTAR has primary text only (gap e1) and the Rising Stars clock rule is unstated (gap e5).

nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.label: All-Star Game team roster strength and composition
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.mechanism: The Game winner is the team whose assigned players are collectively better at scoring in an open-court, low-defence environment, built from impact, shooting and creation of the players who actually appear.
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.rationale: Because the same selected stars are split among teams, gaps are small and dominated by composition: shooters and creators gain more than rim protectors in a low-defence game, and replacements change rosters late. In 2026 teams were built by nationality (USA Stars, USA Stripes, World), so one team can be systematically stronger, unlike a draft; the 2025 team construction behind KXNBAALLSTAR ('Shaq's OGs') was not researched here and is UNVERIFIED.
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.measurement: For each team sum over rostered players minutes_share_i * (0.6*OffImpact_i + 0.25*z(3PA per 36 * 3P%) + 0.15*z(AST%)), where OffImpact_i is multi-season offensive RAPM/EPM shrunk to 0 with prior weight 1,500 possessions; minutes_share from nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan normalised to 1 (the three weights are fixed, not fitted). Output the team difference in impact-weighted points per 100 possessions. Converting it to an expected margin uses a scale factor that is FORMAT-SPECIFIC and is NOT fitted on pooled formats: timed 12-minute games (2026 round robin, one edition: scale UNVERIFIED, use a ridge prior centred on the per-possession rate times roughly 24 possessions per team per 12 minutes with wide uncertainty until more editions exist) and target-score races (margin is replaced by a per-possession edge fed to nba.target_score_race_model) are separate fits; long conventional All-Star Games (2013-2024 style) are only used to estimate the per-possession gap-to-margin relationship, never the margin scale for 12-minute games, and each format uses its own ridge penalty with the number of editions reported. Apply -0.5 point per missing big as a placeholder flagged UNVERIFIED. As-of = final roster after the replacement window; output every team pair.
raw_data: Player offensive impact per 100 possessions (RAPM/EPM or on/off)
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.why: Team strength of the actual All-Star rosters (nationality-built in 2026; the 2025 construction is UNVERIFIED) in a low-defence exhibition is the core input of every exhibition series.

nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.label: All-Star exhibition effort, pace and score variance baseline, conditional on timed vs target format
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.mechanism: Exhibition scoring and margin come from low defensive effort, extreme three-point volume and random clustering of makes; how effort evolves depends on whether the game is clock-timed (2026 All-Star Game: 12-minute games) or a race to a target score (Kalshi text for Rising Stars: first to 40 then 25). The 2025 format behind KXNBAALLSTAR is UNVERIFIED.
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.rationale: Margin variance is large relative to talent gaps, so short games raise the weaker roster's chance. In timed games effort rises in the final minutes and point differential can matter for the tiebreak; in target-score games the end is a race, so the two regimes must not be pooled, and margin SD must never be transferred between formats of different length (a 12-minute game is not a rescaled 48-minute game). The contract year fixes the regime: 2026 KXNBAALLSTARGAME is timed (rules text), KXNBARISINGSTARS is target (rules text); KXNBAALLSTAR 2025 has no format text and was not researched.
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.measurement: Split all exhibition games by format vector from nba.contest_format_rules_ledger. Timed games: points per team per minute, 3PA rate, margin SD per 12 minutes and late-compression coefficient (margin SD change over the final 4 minutes). Target games: points per possession for each team and possessions to reach the target, fed to nba.target_score_race_model. Shrink current-format estimates toward the pooled same-regime value (few games per format); as-of = last completed event; units = points and margin SD.
raw_data: All-Star and Rising Stars team points by period
Lead/score history by minute or play-by-play
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.why: Sets how much randomness separates the stronger team from the weaker one in this exhibition.

nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.label: All-Star Game minutes plan, rest and multi-game fatigue
nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.mechanism: All-Star players play capped minutes with fairly even distribution, and in a multi-game format starters and replacements are managed across games, which changes who is on court in the decisive game.
nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.rationale: Minutes are not set by merit: coaches are mostly told to share minutes, and players with injuries or heavy loads often log little. In a mini-tournament, a team that must play two games may rotate its stars, while the fresh final-game lineup matters more than the roster list.
nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.measurement: For each All-Star in the final roster: rank-based minutes prior m0 = mean All-Star minutes of past players in the same season-minutes tercile and starter/reserve role (2010+), shrunk to the pooled mean with prior weight 10 player-games. Fit a logistic model for P(minutes < 15) on age, season minutes per game (z), starter flag and an injury-flag dummy (Questionable/Probable listed by 24h before tip) with ridge penalty 1.0; for multi-game formats add the fitted game-2 minus game-1 minutes drop by tercile. As-of = last injury-report vintage at least 2 hours before tip; units = minutes and probability of reduced role.
raw_data: All-Star minutes by player and year
nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.why: Needed because the exhibition winner depends on who actually plays and for how long, which can differ sharply from the roster.

nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.label: All-Star / Rising Stars tournament path simulation (round robin, tiebreaks, final)
nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.mechanism: Champion probability is the result of a multi-game path: in 2026 three teams play a round robin of 12-minute games where margins feed the point-differential tiebreak, then the top two play a championship; Rising Stars is a bracket that chains two target-score races (40, 25). Any 2025 All-Star bracket behind KXNBAALLSTAR is UNVERIFIED and not researched.
nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.rationale: A pairwise team gap is not a winner probability: in the 2026 round robin a team's chance depends on its margin distribution in two games (point differential decides a 1-1-1 tie, per rules) and on who it meets in the final; Game 2/3 pairings depend on Game 1's result, so the path is sequential. Which entrants a 2025 bracket had (including any Rising Stars winner as a fourth team) is not established and the simulation must not assume it.
nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.measurement: Monte Carlo (50,000 runs) over the format vector from nba.contest_format_rules_ledger: for timed games draw margin ~ Normal(expected margin from nba.asg_roster_strength_composite adjusted for minutes, SD from nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline); apply the Game-2/Game-3 pairing by Game-1 result; rank by record then point differential and break remaining ties randomly (flagged); play the championship; for target-score formats call nba.target_score_race_model per game. Where the entrant list is not yet announced, draw each entrant from the nba.rising_stars_roster_strength rank order, never from market prices. Output P(champion) and P(final) per team; as-of = last roster change.
free_sources: Format parameters from the rules ledger
Basketball-Reference All-Star box scores for calibration
raw_data: Pairwise expected margins from roster-strength input
nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.why: Directly produces the champion probability that KXNBAALLSTARGAME, KXNBAALLSTAR and KXNBARISINGSTARS settle on.

nba.target_score_race_model.label: Race-to-target exhibition game model (first to 40 / first to 25)
nba.target_score_race_model.mechanism: In a race to a target the winner is the first team to reach or exceed the target score, so the outcome is a first-passage race of two scoring processes rather than a margin over fixed time; whether a clock, time limit or overtime rule also exists is not stated in Kalshi's text and is UNVERIFIED.
nba.target_score_race_model.rationale: A race to 25 has few possessions, so a per-possession efficiency edge converts to a much smaller win probability than in a 48-minute game, and a single three or and-one near the target is decisive (a made shot can overshoot). If there is no clock (the sampled Kalshi text says only 'first team to reach or exceed 40 points', so a time limit is not excluded) there is no garbage time and no clock-driven fouling and timed-game variance estimates do not transfer; a time limit would add a timed branch. Relation to the existing nba.first_passage_race_table: that input is a first-to-N race inside a regular 48-minute game at full effort and does not end the game; here reaching the target ends the game at exhibition effort, so the table is only a structural prior/cross-check for N=25 and is not reused as the estimate.
nba.target_score_race_model.measurement: Model each possession as points in {0,1,2,3,4} with team-specific probabilities from offensive rating vs opponent defence under exhibition effort (from nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline target-regime estimates), alternate possessions with a possession-start Bernoulli, simulate to target T (40 semifinal, 25 final per KXNBARISINGSTARS rules) 20000 times; output P(win) and expected possessions; validate on past target-score exhibitions; units = probability.
free_sources: NBA.com play-by-play of Rising Stars target-score games
League rules sheets (format of earlier All-Star target games UNVERIFIED, not researched)
nba.target_score_race_model.why: Rising Stars (quoted 40/25 targets) is a race, so its winner requires this model; any 2025 All-Star race format is UNVERIFIED and not assumed.

nba.rising_stars_roster_strength.label: Rising Stars team strength from first/second-year and G League rosters
nba.rising_stars_roster_strength.mechanism: Rising Stars teams are drafted from first- and second-year NBA players plus a G League team, so team strength rests on young-player offensive ratings with small samples and a cross-league adjustment for the G League side.
nba.rising_stars_roster_strength.rationale: Rookie and sophomore impact estimates are noisy and the G League team's stats are in a weaker league, so naive per-game scoring over-rates high-usage players on bad teams and mis-rates the G League side. Honorary coaches draft the teams, so team balance depends on the draft, and Rising Stars participants doubling into other events may play reduced minutes.
nba.rising_stars_roster_strength.measurement: Per player: offensive impact per 100 possessions this season (box-score composite) shrunk to a draft-slot prior with weight k = number of possessions at which sampling variance equals prior variance (estimate from rookie seasons 2015-2025, not 800 by assumption). G League players: rating x translation factor estimated as the regression slope of NBA first-year impact on prior G League impact over players who moved between leagues (report the estimate and its se; use 1.0 shrunk toward 0.7 if fewer than 30 players). Team strength = sum over rostered players of minute share x rating with minutes from nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan; output per-possession scoring rate and sd for nba.target_score_race_model. As-of: Rising Stars draft and final roster announcement.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference rookie and G League stats
nba.rising_stars_roster_strength.why: The Rising Stars series settles on these teams (KXNBARISINGSTARS only), which no NBA team rating covers.

interactions.mechanism: Win probability is the roster gap divided by the margin standard deviation, and that deviation is set by game length and late effort, so one and the same gap yields a smaller edge in a 12-minute game than in a 48-minute one and a different edge in a race to 25.
interactions.how_to_test: For every past exhibition compute z = expected gap / SD and compare realised win rates by z bucket and by format length (timed 12 minutes versus target score).

interactions.mechanism: In the three-team round robin a team needs margin only when all three finish 1-1; otherwise wins alone seed the final. A deep team's value therefore switches from win probability to expected point differential in the 1-1-1 branch, and the team that sits out Game 1 plays both remaining games against opponents who have already played.
interactions.how_to_test: In the simulation compare champion probability under win-only ranking and under the point-differential tiebreak, and tag each team's seat (sits out Game 1 or not) to check whether the seat shifts final-appearance frequency in the 2026 data and later editions.

interactions.mechanism: A per-possession edge converts to a win concavely in a race to a small target because few possessions are played; the same Rising Stars roster edge yields a larger win probability in the 40-point semifinal than in the 25-point final, as the 2026 final finished 25-24.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate fixed per-possession edges at targets 25 and 40, then compare with realised favourite win rates in past target-score exhibitions.

interactions.mechanism: A star with a minor injury often plays sharply reduced minutes or none, so the loss to team strength is a threshold at the status tier, not a gradual decline; in a 12-minute game one skipped shift is a large share of his total.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate exhibition minutes by injury-status tier in past editions and test a status-tier discount in the roster composite against a linear one.

interactions.mechanism: With teams built by nationality, the World roster is drawn from a much smaller pool than the two US rosters, so its depth and top-end talent depend on how many internationals the Commissioner adds and on who withdraws; the same star withdrawal costs World more than a US side.
interactions.how_to_test: Rank each nationality roster by the composite and by depth beyond the top three, then compare simulated champion probabilities with and without the injury replacements in 2026 as the only out-of-sample edition.

interactions.mechanism: A team that plays three games (Stars and Stripes in 2026) spends minutes across them, while World played two; late-bracket fatigue and coach minute-sharing change effective strength in the championship game, so the conditional strength of a finalist is not its round-one strength.
interactions.how_to_test: Log minutes per player by game in the 2026 round robin and compare championship-game lineups with pre-tournament plans; repeat in later editions before fitting a fatigue term.

nonlinearities.shape: Regime-dependent: late-game variance compression in timed games, absent in target races
nonlinearities.why: In timed 12-minute games effort rises near the end and lowers final-minute margin variance, while in a target-score race the end is a first-passage threshold (a time limit is not excluded by the sampled text), so the same compression term must be zero there.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at the target with overshoot
nonlinearities.why: The game ends the moment a team reaches 40 or 25, so win probability jumps with a made three or a free throw near the target and possession order matters more than average efficiency; the 2026 final ended 25-24.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating in the number of stars: diminishing returns once minutes are capped
nonlinearities.why: With 12-minute games and minute sharing, adding a further star to the composite adds less than the previous one because the available minutes and shot pool are fixed, so an additive composite overstates deep star rosters.

No margin scale may be pooled across formats of different length: the conventional long All-Star Games supply only a per-possession gap-to-margin relationship, never the 12-minute margin SD.

catalog_entry.label: NBA All-Star exhibition games and Rising Stars tournament winners
catalog_entry.target: Which team wins an All-Star Weekend exhibition game or mini-tournament (All-Star Game, Rising Stars, legends game) under the event's own format.
catalog_entry.mechanism: An All-Star exhibition champion comes from selected or drafted rosters (a nationality split with Commissioner additions in 2026, coach drafts for Rising Stars), the minutes and effort of the players who actually appear in games of only 12 minutes or races to 40 and 25, a single-game conversion with large variance, and a tournament structure (Game-1-dependent pairings, point-differential tiebreak, seeding to a final) that turns single games into a champion. Inputs are scoped per series (KXNBAALLSTARGAME: nationality quota, roster composite, path simulation; KXNBARISINGSTARS: Rising Stars rating and race model; KXNBAALLSTAR: roster composite and path simulation only, its 2025 format being UNVERIFIED) because the formats differ.

inputs.why: Format vector per event-year (game length or target, number of teams, pairing rule, round-robin tiebreak order, roster rule) so every historical label joins to its own format and unverified fields stay flagged.
Team strength of the actual All-Star rosters (nationality-built in 2026, drafted in 2025) in a low-defence exhibition is the core input of every exhibition series.
Exhibition margin variance and late effort set how much of a talent gap converts to a win, separately for timed 12-minute games and untimed races.
Who plays and how many minutes in each game of the format, including fatigue over a second or third game, changes the effective roster.
Round-robin pairing, point-differential tiebreak and bracket simulation turn pairwise team gaps into champion probabilities.
Rising Stars and the 2025 game are races to a target score, which a margin-per-minute model cannot represent.
Rising Stars teams of first/second-year and G League players need their own shrunk, cross-league strength rating.
Selection, captains and participation determine who is eligible for each roster and each event.
Reserve selection and injury replacement set roster membership that feeds roster strength.
The 2026 nationality split (at least 16 US and 8 international players, Commissioner additions) decides how deep the World team is against the two US teams.
Offensive impact ratings feed the roster composite; defensive components are discounted because exhibition defence is minimal.
Three-point volume shapes roster scoring in a high-3PA exhibition; context for the All-Star Game rosters only.
Injury reports before the weekend drive withdrawals, replacements and reduced minutes across all three events.
Announcements of rosters, captains, drafts and format arrive as news before official lists.
Format changes announced by the league (game length, scoring targets, pairing) alter the model for the next edition.
Announcement timing of rosters, drafts and format sets the as-of date for every input.
Rules fix the 12-minute round robin, the 1-1-1 point-differential tiebreak, the 40/25 targets and show where the text is silent.
Official champion announcements are the labels and need reconciling with the contract source.

interactions.hypothesis: Win probability is the roster gap divided by the margin standard deviation, and that deviation is set by game length and late effort, so one and the same gap yields a smaller edge in a 12-minute game than in a 48-minute one and a different edge in a race to 25.
interactions.how_to_test: For every past exhibition compute z = expected gap / SD and compare realised win rates by z bucket and by format length (timed 12 minutes versus target score).

interactions.hypothesis: In the three-team round robin a team needs margin only when all three finish 1-1; otherwise wins alone seed the final. A deep team's value therefore switches from win probability to expected point differential in the 1-1-1 branch, and the team that sits out Game 1 plays both remaining games against opponents who have already played.
interactions.how_to_test: In the simulation compare champion probability under win-only ranking and under the point-differential tiebreak, and tag each team's seat (sits out Game 1 or not) to check whether the seat shifts final-appearance frequency in the 2026 data and later editions.

interactions.hypothesis: A per-possession edge converts to a win concavely in a race to a small target because few possessions are played; the same Rising Stars roster edge yields a larger win probability in the 40-point semifinal than in the 25-point final, as the 2026 final finished 25-24.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate fixed per-possession edges at targets 25 and 40, then compare with realised favourite win rates in past target-score exhibitions.

interactions.hypothesis: A star with a minor injury often plays sharply reduced minutes or none, so the loss to team strength is a threshold at the status tier, not a gradual decline; in a 12-minute game one skipped shift is a large share of his total.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate exhibition minutes by injury-status tier in past editions and test a status-tier discount in the roster composite against a linear one.

interactions.hypothesis: With teams built by nationality, the World roster is drawn from a much smaller pool than the two US rosters, so its depth and top-end talent depend on how many internationals the Commissioner adds and on who withdraws; the same star withdrawal costs World more than a US side.
interactions.how_to_test: Rank each nationality roster by the composite and by depth beyond the top three, then compare simulated champion probabilities with and without the injury replacements in 2026 as the only out-of-sample edition.

interactions.hypothesis: A team that plays three games (Stars and Stripes in 2026) spends minutes across them, while World played two; late-bracket fatigue and coach minute-sharing change effective strength in the championship game, so the conditional strength of a finalist is not its round-one strength.
interactions.how_to_test: Log minutes per player by game in the 2026 round robin and compare championship-game lineups with pre-tournament plans; repeat in later editions before fitting a fatigue term.

unreg:all_star_game_mvp.reviewer: author-blk2-NBA, resolver-blk-NBA (Claude agent; AI, not a human domain expert); fix round

contract.settlement_definition: One series, one player winner. KXNBAALLSTARMVP settles Yes if the named player wins the 2026 Pro Basketball All-Star MVP award; if the player drops out, withdraws or does not participate in the contest for any reason, the market resolves to No (not void). The sampled text does not say who selects the MVP, whether the award covers the whole three-game tournament or only the championship game, how co-winners or ties are handled, or which source decides. Secondary web-search reports (UNVERIFIED: no official description was retrieved) say the 2026 award went to Anthony Edwards of the champion USA Stars on a count reported as 10 of 14 votes with Kawhi Leonard of the runner-up Stripes receiving four, and that fans' votes made up 25%; whether the 14 votes include the fan component is unknown.

rules_evidence.quote: If Brandon Ingram wins the 2026 Pro Basketball All-Star MVP, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: MVP market settles on the official All-Star MVP award for the event; selection method and co-winner handling are unstated.

rules_evidence.quote: If the player drops out, withdraws, or does not participate in the contest for any reason, then the market resolves to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: A named player who withdraws or does not take part resolves No rather than void, so participation probability caps every Yes price and the clause is worded for a contest although the award follows an exhibition game.

variants_and_edge_cases: Withdrawal and non-participation resolve No, including a player who is selected but injured; a replacement named later is a new candidate whose market, if listed, is a separate contract.

Scope: in 2026 the format is a three-game tournament, and the sampled text does not say whether the award is for the whole tournament or the final; reporting suggests the whole tournament (Edwards scored 13, 11 and 8 across the three games) but this is secondary.

Co-MVP and ties are not addressed; the award has historically gone to a single player (not verified here) and secondary reports give the 2026 winner 10 of 14 votes, a split whose composition (media versus fans) is unverified.

Selection method is not in Kalshi's text; secondary reports describe a media panel voting right after the game plus a 25% fan vote, so the settlement source is an official league announcement, not a statistic.

Format comparability: the 2026 award follows a three-game tournament; the format of earlier editions, including 2025 where KXNBAALLSTAR names a team ('Shaq's OGs'), is UNVERIFIED and not researched, so how many earlier MVPs came from a single decision and whether their conditional structure given the winner matches 2026 is unknown.
contract.settlement_data_source: The NBA's official announcement of the All-Star Game MVP (Kobe Bryant Trophy); the sampled rule names no source, so this is assumed and Kalshi's own determination governs if it differs.

mechanism.summary: The MVP is chosen after the exhibition by a vote, not computed from a statistic, so P(a named player wins) factors into four parts. First, he must take part: a withdrawal or non-appearance resolves No, which caps every Yes price at the participation probability. Second, his team must do well in the three-game tournament, because the vote overwhelmingly follows the champion, with a smaller share for a runner-up star. Third, within that team he must post the standout line in capped 12-minute games, which depends on shot share, minutes and the scoring baseline of a no-defence game. Fourth, the voters must pick him: a media panel immediately after the game, plus a reported 25% fan vote, so narrative, home arena and moments weigh alongside points. Each part is discrete and short-sample, so the distribution is concentrated on one or two players once the champion is known, and heavily uncertain before the tournament starts.

stages.name: Participation and replacement
stages.description: A named candidate must be selected, healthy and actually play; injuries, rest and Commissioner replacements change the candidate set up to the day before, and the contract resolves a non-participating player to No rather than void. The probability of appearing is therefore a multiplicative factor in every Yes price and is driven by official status vintages and by reports of who will sit.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli participation per candidate; correlated risk with other weekend events; a status downgrade is a large discrete step.

stages.name: Team result in the tournament
stages.description: Candidates come from teams whose champion probability comes from roster strength, effort and the pairing rule of the three-game format; the champion supplies most MVPs but the runner-up's best player can still collect votes, as the second-place vote in 2026 shows. The path simulation gives each candidate's team the probability of reaching and winning the final.
stages.distribution: Mixture over round-robin and final outcomes; the champion is one of three teams with the seat and the margin tiebreak shaping probabilities.

stages.name: Individual line inside a minute-capped exhibition
stages.description: Given a team result, who posts the standout line depends on shot share, minutes and the scoring baseline: with 12-minute games and minute sharing a player's total across a tournament is bounded, and a team's scoring pool is split among about eight to ten players. Usage and attempt share, not season efficiency, decide who has the opportunity for a 30-point line.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed discrete scoring lines with a hard minutes cap; negatively correlated across teammates through the shared pool.

stages.name: Panel vote
stages.description: A small media panel votes immediately after the final whistle, so recency and the last game carry weight alongside the tournament totals, and narrative (home arena, milestone, farewell) can tilt a choice between similar lines. The panel is small (secondary reports give a 10-of-14 count for the 2026 winner; whether the 14 includes the fan component is unverified), so a single vote moves a share by several percentage points and a split is possible.
stages.distribution: Categorical choice by a handful of voters; ties are possible; a softmax-like concentration on one or two players.

stages.name: Fan ballot and the combined decision
stages.description: Fans' in-game votes reportedly (secondary source, UNVERIFIED weight) count as a quarter of the decision and are a different ballot from the January starter vote; they follow popularity, home market and highlights, and are combined with the panel share into one score. The fan component only changes the winner when the panel is split, so it matters in the close cases that markets price most heavily.
stages.distribution: Share of a quarter-weight categorical vote; correlated with star status and the January ballot rank only as a prior.

stages.name: Settlement of the award
stages.description: The market settles on the officially announced MVP for the stated year, with non-participation resolving to No. The text is silent on the selector, the scope of the award, co-winners and the source, so those are recorded with provenance flags and checked against the league announcement after each edition.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the announcement; ambiguity sits in rare branches such as co-winners or a changed scope.

talent_strength.note: Team strength drives the champion factor and usage drives the individual line.

opponent_matchup.note: No defence or matchup effect shapes an MVP vote in an exhibition; the only opponent effect enters through the team path, which is covered by the tournament simulation.

role_personnel.note: Who plays, for how long and with what shot share.

availability_news.note: Participation is a precondition of the Yes outcome.

coaching_scheme.note: Exhibition coaches set minute sharing only, which is already the minutes-plan input; there is no scheme or tactical choice that shapes an MVP vote beyond that.

environment.note: A neutral site with no travel or altitude effect on a three-game exhibition; the home-arena effect on voters is a narrative factor covered by the narrative input.

game_context_script.note: Tournament path and the scoring baseline of timed exhibition games.

pace_volume.note: Possessions and minutes available to a candidate.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shot share matters more than efficiency in a short exhibition; efficiency luck is mostly noise.

distribution_variance.note: Categorical concentration given the champion and tournament path mixture.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Home market, farewell and popularity effects enter through the narrative and fan inputs; effort differences between players are not measured (gap m3).

officiating_rules.note: The voters are the adjudicators; the ledger holds the voting rule.

settlement_contract.note: One rules text sampled; selector, scope and co-winner handling are flagged unverified.

nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.label: All-Star MVP selection model (production on the winning team and voter choice)
nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.mechanism: The All-Star MVP is chosen by a selection panel after the event; winners almost always come from the champion team and are the standout scorer or narrative figure, so P(MVP) = P(team wins) x P(selected | team wins, box score, narrative).
nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.rationale: The selection method (media panel, any fan component, panel size) and whether the award covers only the championship game or the whole tournament are not in the Kalshi rules, and a withdrawn named player resolves No. Secondary web-search reports for 2026 say the panel votes right after the championship game, fans count 25%, Edwards received 10 of 14 votes and Leonard four, and the award followed the whole three-game tournament; these are UNVERIFIED (no official description was retrieved, and whether the 14 votes include the fan component is unknown). One tournament edition cannot identify weights or covariates.
nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.measurement: P(MVP_i) = P(participates_i) from nba.asg_selectee_nonparticipation_hazard x [ w_panel x PanelShare_i + w_fan x nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share_i ], where w_panel and w_fan are UNVERIFIED parameters (reported 0.75 and 0.25, secondary source only; carry both a reported and an equal-weight scenario until the league's description is read). PanelShare_i = sum over teams P(team wins the tournament) from nba.asg_tournament_path_sim x softmax over that team's players of (b1 x tournament points share + b2 x minutes share), plus a residual mass for a non-champion winner set to the historical share of non-champion MVPs; b1 and b2 are ridge-shrunk toward fixed priors because one three-game edition (2026) and older single-game editions with a different scope cannot identify more than two covariates (home-market and prior-MVP flags enter only as a labelled narrative offset from nba.voting_narrative). The fan share is an independent input and does not take the panel share as input, so the two inputs are not circular; the combination is done only here. As-of: final rosters and participation status.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference All-Star MVP history and box scores
raw_data: Starter status, home-market flag, prior MVP flag
nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.why: MVP is champion probability times the panel's choice among the winning team's players plus a residual for a non-champion winner, combined with the fan ballot at weights that are UNVERIFIED.

nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share.label: All-Star MVP in-game fan vote share (25% of the MVP decision)
nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share.mechanism: The All-Star MVP is reported (secondary, UNVERIFIED) to be decided by a media panel voting right after the championship game plus a fan vote carrying a weight of about 25%; if so, a popular player on the winning team can win with a weaker box score than the panel favourite.
nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share.rationale: Secondary 2026 coverage says fans counted 25% and that the fan vote is cast during the event, separate from the January starter ballot; neither the weight, the mechanics nor any per-player fan returns for the MVP vote were retrieved, so all are UNVERIFIED. The January fan-ballot rank is only a prior for popularity.
nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share.measurement: Per participant: fan_share_i = softmax over the player's team (and then across teams by P(team advances)) of (a x log January All-Star fan-ballot votes + b x tournament points share + c x home-market flag). Per-player fan-vote returns for the in-game MVP ballot are not known to be published (DATA_UNAVAILABLE, gap m4), so a, b and c are UNVERIFIED placeholders (a = 1, b = 2, c = 0.3 inherited from the earlier draft, never estimated) and the output is a labelled prior, not a fitted share. The input does NOT use the panel share or the combined score (the combination w_panel x panel + w_fan x fan lives only in nba.asg_mvp_vote_model), so the pair is acyclic. As-of: final rosters; fan-ballot snapshot dated.
raw_data: All-Star fan-ballot vote totals by player (January returns)
All-Star MVP results and reported vote splits
nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share.why: Carries the in-game fan ballot as a separate, acyclic component whose weight and mechanics are UNVERIFIED; it never takes the panel share as input.

nba.asg_selectee_nonparticipation_hazard.label: All-Star selectee non-participation hazard: P(a selected player does not play in the All-Star event)
nba.asg_selectee_nonparticipation_hazard.mechanism: A selected All-Star can be absent through a pre-event injury or illness withdrawal followed by a Commissioner replacement, a rest decision announced shortly before tip, or an in-event exit; Kalshi resolves the MVP market of a player who drops out, withdraws or does not participate to No, so this probability caps his Yes price.
nba.asg_selectee_nonparticipation_hazard.rationale: The contest-field withdrawal input is calibrated on invited 3PT, dunk and skills entrants announced weeks ahead, a different population; this input is calibrated on All-Star selectees chosen by votes, among whom injured players often attend without playing and replacements are named by the Commissioner. The contract's word 'participate' is unstated for a player who dresses but plays no minutes or leaves after a few seconds.
nba.asg_selectee_nonparticipation_hazard.measurement: Over All-Star selectees 2010-2026 (about 24 to 28 per year, a few hundred player-events): outcome = did not appear in any game of the event. Base rate = (non-participants + 1) / (selectees + 10); logistic update on injury-status tier at the last pre-event report (out, doubtful, questionable, none), games missed in the previous 10 days and a starter-or-reserve flag, ridge penalty 1.0. Add a within-event exit hazard per game for a participant by status tier (UNVERIFIED: only three games exist under the 2026 tournament format). Output P(participates) per named candidate; as-of each injury-report vintage through the day of the game. The boundary of 'participate' (dressed but no minutes, in-game exit) is UNVERIFIED because the contract text says only 'does not participate'.
free_sources: NBA official injury report archive (free, must be archived)
NBA.com All-Star roster and replacement releases
raw_data: All-Star selectees by year with starter or reserve flag
injury status vintages for selectees in the week before the game
minutes played by selectee per event game
nba.asg_selectee_nonparticipation_hazard.why: The MVP market resolves to No for a selectee who does not participate, so P(participates) for All-Star selectees (not contest entrants) multiplies every Yes price.

interactions.mechanism: P(MVP) is roughly P(player's team wins the tournament) times his conditional share of the vote, with a residual for a non-champion winner; a dominant scorer on an underdog team stays priced low while a moderate scorer on the heavy favourite rises, and in a three-team round robin the runner-up's best player can still draw votes.
interactions.how_to_test: Back-test past All-Star MVPs for the fraction from the winning team and fit a conditional logit of selection share given team result and scoring share.

interactions.mechanism: If fans carry a quarter of the decision and the panel carries the rest, a player with a modest panel share but a large fan share can overtake a panel favourite whenever the panel splits; the 2026 panel reportedly split 10-4 between two players, so the fan component matters most when the panel is split.
interactions.how_to_test: Reconstruct combined scores for past MVP votes where both components are published and test how often the fan component changed the winner, conditional on the panel margin.

interactions.mechanism: A star's contribution is capped by the shared minutes and shot pool: once he plays the full allowed minutes and takes the bulk of the team's attempts, extra usage cannot raise his line, so a higher regular-season usage helps less than linearly in a minute-shared exhibition.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress tournament points share on regular-season usage and projected minutes across past editions and test a saturating term against a linear one.

interactions.mechanism: Because non-participation resolves to No, a status downgrade from probable to doubtful removes most of a candidate's Yes value at once, and a late injury replacement creates a new candidate whose MVP probability is small but nonzero.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare final-day price-independent participation rates by status tier in past All-Star rosters and test whether replacements ever won the award.

interactions.mechanism: Fans can only vote for what they see: a player who plays the allowed minutes in all three games has three games of visible moments, while a star who plays one short game or sits the final has few, so the fan component's reach depends on minutes and appearances (a measurable variable), not on a general narrative.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress the share of reported in-game fan or panel support on minutes played and games appeared in past All-Star events where either is published, and compare the slope for starters and reserves.

nonlinearities.shape: Winner-takes-most concentration within the champion team
nonlinearities.why: Within the champion roster the vote concentrates on one or two players through a softmax-like choice, so a modest edge in scoring share turns into a large edge in selection probability while deep reserves have almost no chance whatever their share.

With 12-minute games and minute-sharing, shot share cannot keep rising with usage once a player is on the floor for the maximum allowed time, so the relation between regular-season usage and an exhibition scoring line flattens for high-usage stars.
Because non-participation resolves No, every Yes probability is capped by the probability that the selectee plays, which drops sharply with an injury status change rather than gradually.

unresolved.description: How the 2026 All-Star MVP is selected (media panel size, the fan share reported as 25%, the reported 10-of-14 count, and whether the award covers the whole three-game tournament) comes only from secondary web-search reports; the league's own description of the voting could not be retrieved because nba.com does not resolve from the research session, and the media/fan split of the 14 votes is not given.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Read the NBA's 2026 MVP announcement and voting description and record panel size, fan weight and scope in the format ledger with provenance.

unresolved.description: KXNBAALLSTARMVP's text names only withdrawal-to-No (worded for a 'contest'); it does not state the selector, the scope (tournament or final), co-MVP handling, the meaning of 'participate' or the source of truth, and the format of earlier editions, including 2025, was not researched and is UNVERIFIED.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Obtain Kalshi's clarification or the full rulebook entry for the MVP series and check each past edition for scope.

unresolved.description: The effect of home arena, narrative and effort differences on the panel and fan vote cannot be measured with a pregame variable defined here, and only a handful of editions exist under the 2026 three-game tournament scope.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Collect the voting breakdown for several editions and test narrative proxies (home market, milestone, prior MVP) against selection residuals.

unresolved.description: Per-player in-game fan-vote returns for the MVP ballot and the exact weight of the fan component are not shown to be published anywhere; nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share therefore runs on unestimated placeholder parameters (a = 1, b = 2, c = 0.3) and only a labelled prior can be produced.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Locate published per-player fan counts or shares for past MVP ballots, or obtain the league's description of the fan component, before any parameter is fitted.

unresolved.description: The panel-choice model cannot be identified from the data that exist: one three-game tournament edition (2026) and older editions with a different scope give only a handful of outcomes, so any conditional logit with more than two covariates is under-identified and weights are not estimable.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Report the effective number of editions, fit with the two-covariate ridge prior only, and defer richer covariates until more tournament editions exist.

nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.reason: Champion and finalist probabilities per team are the first factor of P(MVP); in 2026 the MVP came from the champion but the runner-up's players also drew votes, so path probabilities for both finalists are needed.

nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.reason: Bounds each candidate's minutes across a multi-game tournament of 12-minute games; a secondary driver because the vote responds to points and moments more than to minutes themselves.

nba.voting_narrative.reason: Narrative effects (home arena, farewell, milestone) move the panel among comparable lines, but the effect size is unmeasured and the electorate is small.

nba.usage.reason: Shot share inside the exhibition decides who posts the standout line; regular-season usage is only a rough proxy in a no-defence format with minute-sharing.

nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.reason: Used to get P(champion) and the share of tournament scoring each player can reach; the primary role belongs to the path simulation.

nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.reason: Sets the scale of the top individual scoring line in a timed 12-minute game; matters because the panel responds to a standout line.

nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.reason: Calibrated on invited 3PT, dunk and skills entrants announced weeks ahead, the wrong population for the MVP clause, which needs the probability that an All-Star selectee does not play; replaced for this archetype by nba.asg_selectee_nonparticipation_hazard.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Participation and minutes depend on status vintages released through the day before; the sharpest pregame information for an MVP market.

nba.news.reason: Replacement announcements and process news arrive in reporting before official lists; weigh by reporter reliability.

nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.reason: Holds the MVP selection method, weights and scope (whole tournament versus final) as provenance-flagged fields; without it the conditional structure of the award is unknown.

catalog_entry.label: NBA All-Star Game MVP
catalog_entry.target: Which player is named the NBA All-Star Game MVP.
catalog_entry.mechanism: The All-Star MVP is a voted award: P(a named player) is the probability he participates, times the probability his team wins the tournament, times his conditional share of a media-panel and fan vote that follows the standout scoring line, minutes and narrative in minute-capped exhibition games, plus a residual for a runner-up player. Withdrawal resolves No, and the selector, scope and co-winner handling are not in Kalshi's text.

inputs.why: The MVP is the combined panel-and-fan outcome conditional on which team wins; this model is P(champion) times the panel's choice among that team's players plus a residual for a non-champion winner.
Carries the in-game fan ballot (reported as 25% of the decision in 2026) as a separate component from the panel and from the January starter vote.
Champion and finalist probabilities per team come from the tournament simulation, and MVP probability is capped by the player's team path.
Minutes inside capped 12-minute games bound how many points and moments a player can accumulate across the tournament.
Home-market, farewell and storyline effects shift the panel and fan choice among comparable stat lines.
Shot share inside the exhibition decides who posts the standout line, and it is the best pregame proxy for who will take the shots.
Team strength feeds P(champion) and the share of the scoring pool available to each player.
The exhibition scoring baseline and variance decide how large the top individual line can be in a timed game.
The MVP rule resolves a non-participating named player to No, so the probability that an All-Star selectee does not play (not contest-field withdrawal) multiplies every Yes price.
Injury status before the game drives both participation and minutes, which cap a candidate's chance.
Announcements of rosters, replacements and the voting process arrive as news before official lists.
Records the MVP selection method, panel and fan weights and whether the award covers the whole tournament or the final, each with its provenance flag.
Announcement timing of rosters and the voting method sets the as-of date for every input.
Changes to the format or the MVP process announced by the league alter the conditional structure of the award.
The rules fix withdrawal-to-No and show that the selection method, co-MVP handling and source are not stated.
The official MVP announcement is the label and must be reconciled with the contract source.

interactions.hypothesis: P(MVP) is roughly P(player's team wins the tournament) times his conditional share of the vote, with a residual for a non-champion winner; a dominant scorer on an underdog team stays priced low while a moderate scorer on the heavy favourite rises, and in a three-team round robin the runner-up's best player can still draw votes.
interactions.how_to_test: Back-test past All-Star MVPs for the fraction from the winning team and fit a conditional logit of selection share given team result and scoring share.

interactions.hypothesis: If fans carry a quarter of the decision and the panel carries the rest, a player with a modest panel share but a large fan share can overtake a panel favourite whenever the panel splits; the 2026 panel reportedly split 10-4 between two players, so the fan component matters most when the panel is split.
interactions.how_to_test: Reconstruct combined scores for past MVP votes where both components are published and test how often the fan component changed the winner, conditional on the panel margin.

interactions.hypothesis: A star's contribution is capped by the shared minutes and shot pool: once he plays the full allowed minutes and takes the bulk of the team's attempts, extra usage cannot raise his line, so a higher regular-season usage helps less than linearly in a minute-shared exhibition.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress tournament points share on regular-season usage and projected minutes across past editions and test a saturating term against a linear one.

interactions.hypothesis: Because non-participation resolves to No, a status downgrade from probable to doubtful removes most of a candidate's Yes value at once, and a late injury replacement creates a new candidate whose MVP probability is small but nonzero.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare final-day price-independent participation rates by status tier in past All-Star rosters and test whether replacements ever won the award.

interactions.hypothesis: Fans can only vote for what they see: a player who plays the allowed minutes in all three games has three games of visible moments, while a star who plays one short game or sits the final has few, so the fan component's reach depends on minutes and appearances (a measurable variable), not on a general narrative.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress the share of reported in-game fan or panel support on minutes played and games appeared in past All-Star events where either is published, and compare the slope for starters and reserves.
